<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Test first: red, green, refactor", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Pick ONE acceptance criterion. Say it in one line.
2. Write one test for it, in the project's tests folder, named like the tests already there.
3. Run the test command. It must FAIL because of an assertion, not an import or syntax error. Copy the failing line.
4. Write the smallest code that makes it pass.
5. Run the same command again. Copy the runner's summary line, for example `3 passed`.
6. Tidy up without changing behaviour, then run the whole suite.
7. Go back to step 1 for the next criterion.
## Checklist
- [ ] Every criterion has a test that failed before it passed.
- [ ] The whole suite passes in this run.
- [ ] No existing test was edited or deleted to make it pass.
## Definition of done
The test runner's own summary line shows all tests passing, and you saw each new test fail first.
## Verify
Find the test command in `docs/knowledge/how-to-run.md`, else use `python -m pytest -q` or `npm test` if present. Run it from the project's top folder.
## Common mistakes
- An import error counted as the failing test: fix the import and run again until an assertion fails.
- Changing the test until it passes: change the code instead.
- Writing "tests pass" without running them: run the command and quote the line.
- Writing all the code before the first test: go back to step 2.
## Example
Criterion: an order of 100 costs 90. Test: `assert total([100]) == 90`. Run: `1 failed` with `assert 100 == 90`. Fix `total`. Run: `1 passed`.
